leads.question: Which detailed player-reported mechanics in cabbagery's 2024 recollection are accurate, and which can be promoted into durable behavioral fixtures or subsystem documentation?
leads.next_discriminator: Reproduce the claims independently against the canonical ROM/runtime in small slices: (1) enumerate Hunter path-crossing effects and trigger behavior; (2) verify Hunter unlock propagation into 2P/versus/league and whose progression state gates it; (3) verify top-three record persistence and identity/color mutation after overwriting a racer; (4) characterize stunt scoring on Downer and adjacent stunt courses using deterministic inputs; (5) map rejected-name behavior to the existing forbidden-name evidence; (6) verify Anti-Uni/Neon endgame gating. Promote only locally reproduced facts.
deliverables: Hunter crossing-effect behavior matrix with deterministic reproduction
Hunter multiplayer unlock/gating observation
record-orphaning fixture covering racer overwrite and retained record value
bounded stunt-scoring characterization for Downer plus one comparison course
forbidden-name cross-check against existing ROM/achievement/patch evidence
Anti-Uni and Neon progression-gating observation
promoted symbols/tests/docs only for confirmed claims
leads.acquisition_judgment: High-value because the claims are concrete and cheaply falsifiable. Do not treat recollection as authority; use it to seed canonical-ROM/runtime experiments.

leads.question: Which community-documented mechanics recur across independent sources strongly enough to justify direct canonical-ROM/runtime tests and durable fixtures?
leads.next_discriminator: Prioritize independently repeated, implementation-relevant claims: stunt score values/decay, boost gain and offscreen depletion, track-color cue semantics, Hunter/Anti-Uni effect triggers, screen-position/scrolling influence on race timing, Mega stunt detection, and rejected-name substring behavior. For each claim, build the cheapest deterministic reproduction and record corroborating versus conflicting sources before promotion. Also verify TAS-reported Tabletop duration-dependent scoring and whether airborne stunt input remains active after the stunt timer reaches zero.
deliverables: cross-source mechanics concordance table
deterministic stunt-score and repeat-decay fixture
boost/offscreen depletion measurement
screen-position/scrolling timing discriminator
Mega stunt recognition fixture
name-filter substring behavior fixture
source conflict notes where player recollections disagree
Tabletop duration-scoring and stunt-timer overrun fixture
leads.acquisition_judgment: High leverage because multiple independent player/research communities describe overlapping mechanics; canonical reproduction can turn folklore into durable regression tests cheaply.

leads.question: Does race-speed boost scale with stunt complexity/count, or is each successful stunt effectively a fixed boost with apparent differences coming from landing quality, timing, offscreen depletion, or combo structure?
leads.next_discriminator: Build deterministic same-course traces comparing single Twist, single Roll, Flip, Roll+Twist, Double Flip, and Flip City from matched pre-jump state. Measure resulting speed/boost state frame-by-frame through landing and for a fixed post-landing window, both onscreen and offscreen. Separate stunt-score value from race-speed boost and landing penalty.
deliverables: frame-level boost/speed comparison matrix
landing-quality penalty characterization
onscreen/offscreen depletion comparison
resolved source-conflict note with canonical behavior
leads.acquisition_judgment: High value because independent experienced-player sources disagree on a core racing mechanic. Cheap deterministic measurement should settle it.

leads.question: Which malformed SRAM states can reproduce historically reported name, score, palette, or startup corruption, and how should the modern host/profile layer fail safely around them?
leads.next_discriminator: Use known SRAM structure and existing profile/save tooling to generate bounded corruptions around racer identity, score tables, and nearby metadata. Reproduce only project-owned synthetic cases; do not assume the forum-reported battery/root-cause theory. Verify stock behavior where practical, then ensure modern Windows profile handling detects or contains malformed state without silently damaging unrelated profiles.
deliverables: synthetic malformed-SRAM fixture set
stock-behavior observations for recoverable corruption classes
modern profile/save containment expectations
explicit separation of observed symptoms from unproven hardware/root-cause claims
leads.acquisition_judgment: Useful because it turns real historical failure symptoms into bounded robustness tests for the modern save/profile layer.

leads.question: What is the orange fallback/recovery track space, and which collision/state transitions allow the player to enter, bypass, or escape it?
leads.next_discriminator: Reproduce the three player-described escape families on canonical runtime: vertical-jump floor penetration, seat-impact escape at orange-zone arrows, and turnaround-zone bypass. Capture course position, collision mode, track-piece identity, camera/screen state and finishability before/after each transition. Determine whether 'orange track' is ordinary authored recovery geometry, a generic fallback path, or a distinct engine state.
deliverables: reproducible input traces for each confirmed escape family
orange-track geometry/state classification
collision/state transition trace across normal -> fallback -> normal or broken state
fixture for at least one recoverable escape and one non-finishable/corrupted path if canonical behavior confirms them
documentation separating player terminology from engine-confirmed semantics
leads.acquisition_judgment: High-value because the source describes concrete, reproducible geometry escapes that can expose hidden recovery-track and collision-state semantics.

leads.question: How exactly does the stock handicap/rubberband system depend on racer separation, screen position, opponent class, and circuit/race mode?
leads.next_discriminator: Use deterministic traces that intentionally fall behind then recover, measuring racer speed/boost, opponent state, screen-X position and lap time against matched no-handicap controls. Reproduce the historical strategy of letting Bronzen get ahead for unusually fast circuit laps and distinguish player handicap from camera/scroll effects.
deliverables: handicap activation/deactivation thresholds
player/opponent speed effect matrix
interaction with screen position and scrolling
validated or rejected historical low-time strategy
fixture guarding handicap semantics
leads.acquisition_judgment: Core racing behavior repeatedly mentioned by competitive players and reviews; inexpensive deterministic measurement can resolve it.

acquisition_policy.rule: Keep all leads searchable, but do not let low marginal-value artifacts block implementation or reverse engineering.

tiers.P0: active hunt; likely to materially reduce implementation uncertainty
tiers.P1: useful corroboration; pursue opportunistically or with cheap automation
tiers.P2: optional evidence; acquire if easy, never block
tiers.P3: archival tail; preserve lead, no bespoke recovery effort unless a new discriminator raises its value
